title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI hooks for regression and quality gating
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: we need stronger guardrails to prevent prompt-set regressions from reaching production. This PR adds per-prompt CI hooks and quality gating to the eval-harness so that PRs can fail fast on regressions for critical prompt-sets and surface prompt-level metrics to reviewers. Summary: adds a new eval runner invoked from GitHub Actions that computes per-prompt metrics (accuracy, pass-rate, BLEU/EM where applicable, and a new prompt-level quality score). The runner uploads a compact diff report and a machine-readable artifact to the PR; the CI hook evaluates those results against per-prompt thresholds defined in eval-harness/config/prompts.yaml. If any critical prompt falls below its threshold the job fails and posts an actionable comment. What this changes: - eval-harness/core: new reporter and per-prompt aggregator code. - eval-harness/ci: GitHub Actions workflow and helper script to fetch baseline artifacts. - eval-harness/config: prompts.yaml schema update to include severity and fail-on-regression flags. - docs: usage and ops runbook for tuning thresholds and interpreting diffs. Checklist: - [x] implement per-prompt aggregator and metric exporters - [x] add GH action for PR evaluation - [x] add gating rules and default thresholds for existing prompt-sets - [x] integration tests for the runner - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] add examples for how to add new prompt thresholds Testing: unit tests for aggregator logic included. Integration workflow runs against a staged baseline (mocked model outputs) to validate failure/success transitions. Manual verification performed on a handful of recent PRs that previously caused regressions. Notes and caveats: - Default thresholds are conservative and can be overridden in the prompts.yaml per-team. - The CI job is opt-in for very large prompt-sets via an allow-list to avoid long runs on small tooling PRs. - This initial implementation focuses on scalar metrics; future work will add distributional tests and prompt-level embeddings-based similarity checks. Related: ENG-3412 tracks adding per-prompt alerts to Console; SUP-4321 surfaced early support requests that motivated stricter gating.

review_comments: Diego Rivera: Can we make the fail-on-regression rules namespace-aware so teams can opt out? Response: yes - added a per-team allow_list and made the workflow opt-in for non-critical sets.
Priya Nair: The default thresholds look aggressive for smaller prompt-sets. Response: lowered defaults for prompt-sets < 50 examples and documented how to tune thresholds in the runbook.
Samir Gupta: Will this add significant CI runtime? Response: added caching and a quick-fail path - most PRs hit the allow-list fast; we also limit full runs to a single shard by default.

Priya Nair: Request to include a compact artifact for programmatic consumption by the Console alerts team. Response: added JSON artifact upload (artifact key: per_prompt_diff.json) and a signed download URL in the PR comment.
ci_checks: integration-eval (workflow): initial run flaky -> rerun passed
release_notes: Add per-prompt CI hooks and quality gating to eval-harness. CI now evaluates prompt-level regressions and fails PRs when critical prompts drop below configured thresholds. Includes reporter, GH Action, and docs.
notes_for_ops: Ops: thresholds live in eval-harness/config/prompts.yaml. To add or tune prompt thresholds open a Linear task and update the config; Console alerts will subscribe to the per_prompt_diff.json artifact once ENG-3412 is complete.
